24bab0002794.verifyAtPunch: Run the shower at a comfortable setting, then flush the toilet in the same room while it runs — the shower temperature must not spike; then run the lavatory hot and confirm the same. Confirm the trim is the pressure-balancing model, not a plain mixer.
24bab0002794.src: A530 keyed note 14 (placed on views 04 and 05); P104 REMARKS rows SH-3/SH-4; P202/P305 (120 F HWS distribution); P301/P305 (TMV scoped to public lavs)
24bab0002794.label: On/off PRESSURE-BALANCING (anti-scald) valve - P104 gives the guestroom rows SH-3 / SH-4 only 'Delta T24859 supply'; NO valve or cartridge model is printed for the guestroom
24bab0002794.instanceNote: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT OPERATING TEST IN THIS BATHROOM. Guestroom HWS is distributed at 120 F per P202/P305 and there is NO guestroom thermostatic mixing valve scheduled — P301/P305's 110 F TMV note is scoped to PUBLIC lavatories and hand sinks — so this pressure-balancing valve is the ONLY temperature protection at the shower. A530 keyed note 14 reads verbatim 'ON/OFF - PRESSURE BALANCING VALVE' and is placed on views 04 and 05. Confirm it is a pressure-balancing valve, not a plain mixer. No control height is dimensioned on A530 for the standard rooms (the 8"-10" band and MAX dims belong to the accessible sheets A532/A532.1 and do not apply here).

f47c51e4b579.verifyAtPunch: Press TEST then RESET — it must trip, reset, and actually kill the receptacle (confirm with a plug tester, not the indicator light); measure to the device centreline and write the number down; record whether this outlet carries the night light.
f47c51e4b579.src: A530 keyed note 13 (placed on view 03); G402 schedule general note 6; A530 keyed note 24; E400 Panel A/B bathroom-GFCI circuit + panel note 4; E101 spec #25 (TR in guestrooms/baths) and #18; A530 general note D; G400 detail 02
f47c51e4b579.where: Bath, on a SIDEWALL of the lavatory / water basin (G402 schedule note 6) — not the wall behind the basin. May share a 4x4 box and one plate with the bath light switch (G402 bath GN1, E400 GN2)
f47c51e4b579.instanceNote: Device presence is certain — A530 keyed note 13 ('GFCI OUTLET') is PLACED on A530 view 03, the door/shower wall of the bathroom that governs this room. THE MOUNTING HEIGHT IS AN OPEN CONFLICT: 12" (A530 GENERAL NOTES note D, verbatim 'A.F.F. WALL RECEPTACLES/DATA PORTS TO [B]E MOUNTED @ 12" TYPICAL U.N.O', byte-identical on A531, A532, A532.1 and A533) vs 18" (E101 spec #18, E101 symbol legend, G400 detail 02 'ALL RECEPTACLES SHALL BE 18" A.F.F. UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE'). RECORD the height, do not judge it (coordination_issues C-03). ALSO CHECK HERE, NOT ONLY AT THE SWITCH: A530 keyed note 24 permits the LED night light to be integrated with EITHER the light switch OR the outlet — if the switch has no night light, look at this device before writing anything up. Finally: E400 panel note 4 calls a GFCI BREAKER — do NOT accept a GFCI breaker as a substitute for a GFCI device at the receptacle without an EOR answer.
f47c51e4b579.label: Bathroom GFCI duplex receptacle, tamper-resistant, 20 A

121591af18d1.where: Bathroom ceiling at the exhaust inlet — if it is a physical in-room fan at all
121591af18d1.instanceNote: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE READINGS — THE QUANTITY MAY BE 1 OR ZERO. M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic ceiling fan (remarks 1 brick vent, 2 ceiling radiation damper, 3 'switch w/ room lights', 5 backdraft damper, 6 off-white aluminium grille, 9 UL/Energy Star/AMCA); M202 and M301-M304 repeat it. But M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + Aldes regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 to EF-11 — no in-room fan anywhere. A grille-only inlet and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. Supporting but not conclusive: E400's Panel A/B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit (though remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit and need no breaker). coordination_issues C-06 — a 115-unit buy. DO NOT order 115 Panasonic on this. SECOND, SEPARATE TWO-READING CONFLICT ON THE SWITCHING, both carried: M201 remark 3 says the fan is switched WITH the room lights; G402's guestroom-bath general note 3 says verbatim 'CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT'. Record which way it is wired; do not write either up. SETTLES IT FASTEST: this walk — look behind the grille in this room.
121591af18d1.label: Toilet exhaust fan — M201 schedules Panasonic FV-0511VK2, ceiling, 50 CFM, 115/1/60, with backdraft damper
121591af18d1.verifyAtPunch: Drop the bath grille and look — record 'fan housing' or 'bare duct to riser', with a photo. Then flip the bath light switch and record whether the fan runs with the light or on a separate switch. That single observation closes C-06.
121591af18d1.src: M201 EF-1 row + remark codes 1/2/3/5/6/9; M202; M301-M304; against M305 EV riser diagrams; E400 Panel A/B circuit list; G402 guestroom-bath general note 3; coordination_issues C-06

76c7a39e2de0.instanceNote: QUANTITY MAY BE 1 OR ZERO IN THIS ROOM — 1 is a placeholder. THREE GAPS ON ONE ITEM. (1) PLACEMENT UNKNOWN: P401/P402 restrict SK-3/SK-4 verbatim to 'the suite/extended units' and assign it to NONE of their seven unit plans. Floor 1 has no King One Bedroom suites and no QQ Extended rooms, so a literal reading gives ZERO kitchenette sinks on floor 1 including this room — while the 'every Home2 key is a suite' reading gives all 16. The sheets support both and settle neither. (2) NO SCHEDULED PRODUCT: SK-3 and SK-4 appear nowhere in P104 (only SK-1/SK-2, both Elkay laundry sinks); the S4 product data fills the hole rather than superseding a sheet. (3) THE FAUCET IS THE WRONG TYPE ON ITS FACE: Moen 8227's own product sheet titles it 'Two-Handle LAVATORY Faucet with Spout', 8" widespread, 3-HOLE — it will not drop into a single-hole kitchenette deck, and the PEKOE sink requires a 26" cabinet. A dishwasher (902) tagged with no drawn sink is itself an RFI, and one is already open — do not raise a second. NOTE THE INTERLOCK: the dishwasher-switch line above depends on this — no sink means no under-sink cabinet.
76c7a39e2de0.where: Entry / kitchenette leg, if provided — note A555 view 01 tags 901 REFRIGERATOR and 902 DISHWASHER on the working wall and tags NO SINK
76c7a39e2de0.label: Kitchenette / wet-bar sink and faucet — American Standard PEKOE 23x18 single-bowl stainless undermount 18SB.10231800.075 + Moen 8227
76c7a39e2de0.src: P401/P402 (marks SK-3/SK-4, 'suite/extended units', assigned to no unit plan); P104 (schedules no product for either mark); S4 product data (American Standard 18SB.10231800.075; Moen 8227)
76c7a39e2de0.verifyAtPunch: Record PRESENT or ABSENT in the kitchenette leg with a photo; if present, count the deck holes, write down which faucet was installed, run it hot and cold for 60 seconds and wipe the trap and both stops for weep.

7bc0ef08a698.instanceNote: DB GAP AND A PARTLY UNSTATED ITEM — carried IN because Austin asked for anything electrical in the rooms and because the far end of a dedicated circuit is a punch-visible device. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: E400 lists 'refrigerator' among the per-room power items and E400/E103 schedule a dedicated Refrigerator circuit at 173 VA on every guestroom panel; A555 view 01 tags 901 REFRIGERATOR on the working wall; the S3 cutsheet is a Danby DFF101B1BSSDB, 115 V / 160 W. CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT, which called it 'cord-and-plug connected': the cutsheet says no such thing. The S3 dishwasher rows state the connection in terms ('attached power cord' on the 18", 'power cord sold separately, spare part 17476000000137' on the 24"); the refrigerator row states NOTHING about the connection — which is precisely why this line exists. WHAT IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE: no keynote, no symbol and no dimension places this receptacle, no sheet gives its height, and no sheet says whether the connection is a receptacle or a hard-wired appliance connection (E101's symbol legend carries both a duplex receptacle and an 'electrical connection to appliance/equipment' symbol). DO NOT write up a height or a device type against a number no sheet prints. RECORD what is there. SETTLES IT: pull the device symbol at the refrigerator position off the A555 view 04.1 / E400 PDF at full scale.
7bc0ef08a698.where: Working wall / kitchenette leg, behind or beside the 901 refrigerator position tagged on A555 view 01
7bc0ef08a698.label: Refrigerator receptacle / appliance connection at the working wall (901 REFRIGERATOR, Danby DFF101B1BSSDB, 115 V / 160 W)
7bc0ef08a698.src: E400 per-room power list ('refrigerator') + Panel A/B Refrigerator circuit; E103 refrigerator 173 VA column; A555 view 01 tag 901; A550 furnishings legend 901 = REFRIGERATOR; S3 Danby DFF101B1BSSDB cutsheet (115 V / 160 W — states no connection type); E101 symbol legend
7bc0ef08a698.verifyAtPunch: Pull the refrigerator forward — record whether it is plugged into a receptacle or hard-wired, record the receptacle height and whether it is TR, plug-test it for polarity and ground, and confirm the refrigerator runs.

67f2c0e6e772.verifyAtPunch: Drop the grille and look up the neck for a damper with a locking quadrant — record present/absent and whether the quadrant is set and locked rather than wired or taped shut.
67f2c0e6e772.src: M401 (EAG-50 shown with VD and FD); M101 legend (Manual Volume Damper VD) + GN26 (locking quadrant); M301 GN11 (balancing damper each branch/runout); M101 GN7 (min 12"x12" access to dampers)
67f2c0e6e772.label: Volume damper at the toilet exhaust, with a locking quadrant
67f2c0e6e772.instanceNote: ARGUABLE SCOPE CALL, STATED SO AUSTIN CAN OVERRULE. If the VD sits at the grille neck it is reachable by dropping the EAG-50 and is plainly IN. If it sits further up the branch it is above a 7'-3" hard painted-gyp lid with NO access panel drawn on any guestroom RCP, and it becomes unreachable rough-in. No sheet says which. Carried IN because the damper's EFFECT is tested at a visible point — the airflow reading at the grille — and because M101 GN7 requires access to it in either case. CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT: M101 GN25 was cited and has been struck — GN25 reads 'Each SUPPLY outlet gets its own balancing device' and the EAG-50 is an EXHAUST grille, so GN25 does not reach it. The citation that does is M301 general note 11 (balancing damper each branch/runout) plus M101 GN26 (manual balancing dampers have locking quadrant). SETTLES IT: drop one grille and look, plus the same RFI that asks for the missing bath access panel.
67f2c0e6e772.where: At the toilet exhaust branch — position not dimensioned by M401

6ef92634a059.verifyAtPunch: Plug a laptop in at the desk grommet and confirm link and a DHCP address; record which option you found — a real jack, a patch cord run from the WAP port, or nothing at all.
6ef92634a059.src: A555 keynote 46 (views 04/04.1); A550 legend keynote 46 full text; A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'OPTIONAL DATA'
6ef92634a059.instanceNote: NARROWED FROM THE DB'S FLAG — THE SHEETS DO SAY MORE THAN THE DB NOTE ADMITS. 'Optional' in keynote 46 does NOT mean optional whether to install; it names two alternative ways to deliver it, verbatim: 'OPTION WIRED DATA CONNECTION FOR GUEST USE: A) ADD CAT6 RJ-45 CABLE JACK AND PATCH CORD THROUGH DESKTOP GROMMET - OR - B) PATCH CORD FROM WAP PORT THROUGH DESKTOP GROMMET.' Keynote 46 IS in A555's placed-keynote list for views 04/04.1 and 'OPTIONAL DATA' is its own symbol on the power & signal legend, so something lands at the grommet here. WHAT IS UNSTATED is which of A or B was bought — option A is a real jack and a genuine x115 cost item, option B is near-zero cost. Under either option a guest must get a working wired connection at the desk, so the walker cannot mis-punch it. SETTLES IT: the low-voltage integrator's submittal or an owner/franchise direction. Do NOT write 'nothing' up as a defect until scope is answered.
6ef92634a059.where: At the desktop grommet on the working-wall desk
6ef92634a059.label: Optional wired data connection at the desktop grommet — CAT6 jack + patch cord (A), or a patch cord from the WAP port (B)

c6d0d5e83883.verifyAtPunch: Read the nameplate model off the unit and write it down; run heat and then cool from the wall control and confirm discharge changes temperature at the grille.
c6d0d5e83883.src: M201 PTAC schedule (PTAC-1 AZ65H12DAB / PTAC-2 AZ65H15DAB, OSA 45.0 CFM both); M401 det.01 + KN3 + KN7; M301 line 30; M501 det.9; A555 KN1 view 08
c6d0d5e83883.label: Packaged terminal A/C unit, G.E., 208/1/60, in through-wall sleeve — PTAC-1 = AZ65H12DAB (11,900 BTU/h cool) / PTAC-2 = AZ65H15DAB (14,200 BTU/h cool)
c6d0d5e83883.instanceNote: WHICH UNIT IS UNRESOLVED FOR THIS ROOM. 101 is QQ family, so it falls in M401 detail 01 (QQ, QQ Ext., QQ Conn.) and M401 line 24 states verbatim that details 01/02 show PTAC-2. M301 line 30 states verbatim 'PTAC-1 at all 16 first-floor guestrooms.' Mutually exclusive; M401 KN7 itself defers location to M201/M301-M304, which argues for M301, but M401's own detail contradicts it. Also: NO SHEET PRINTS THE COMPOSITE STRING 'PTAC-2 / PTAC-1' — M201 schedules the two as separate rows with different models and capacities; the composite is the DB's carry-both convention (packages/mechanical.md flag F4) and must not be treated as a printed tag on a purchase document. SETTLES IT: read the nameplate on the walk — AZ65H12DAB = PTAC-1, AZ65H15DAB = PTAC-2. That one reading closes F4 for this room. CORRECTED: the DB row cited 'A555 KN1/KN30 view 08'; A555 view 08 carries keynotes 1 and 4 ONLY and A555 never places keynote 30 anywhere — KN30 struck from this row.
c6d0d5e83883.where: Exterior window wall, under the window, ST-01 quartz stool over it (A555 view 08)

8672399f567a.instanceNote: DB GAP AND THE MOST-TOUCHED DEVICE IN THE ROOM — the draft carried a bath switch and a disposal switch and nothing else, and told the walker to 'confirm each switches' with no device line to record against. THE SWITCHES EXIST: E400 lists per-room 'switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)'; the A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND — printed on the sheet that governs this room — includes 'SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY'; and A555 keynote 3 restricts the night-light switch to 'IN BATHROOM LOCATIONS ONLY', which only makes sense if switches exist outside the bath. WHAT IS NOT STATED: the COUNT (the symbol is a graphic on A555 view 04.1 — pull it off the PDF at full scale before the walk; qty 1 here is a placeholder, not a count), WHAT EACH CONTROLS, and the HEIGHT, which carries the same four-value conflict as the bath switch: 54" (E101 spec #18) vs 48" (E101's own symbol legend) vs 3'-10" = 46" (G400 detail 02, 'SWITCH ... (UNO)') vs the 15"-48" guest-control band in A530 general note F, which is printed unqualified and reaches this room. NOT APPLICABLE HERE: G400 detail 02's 3-way WELCOME light switch at 2'-5" is scoped verbatim to 'ACCESSIBLE GUESTROOMS @ BED LOCATION' and 101 is not accessible; A550/A555 keynote 35 (switches controlling mechanical shades) does not apply either — 101 has GR-400 MANUAL shades per A555 keynote 4. MEASURE AND RECORD; do not write a height up.
8672399f567a.where: Entry leg at the guestroom door, and wherever else A555 view 04.1 dimensions a switch symbol
8672399f567a.label: Entry / room lighting switch(es) — count, location and height not stated on any sheet
8672399f567a.verifyAtPunch: Operate every switch in the room and write down what each one controls; count them and record the number; measure to the top of each and write the numbers down against 46" / 48" / 54"; confirm any 3-way pair works from both positions.
8672399f567a.src: E400 ('switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)'); A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY'; A555 keynote 3 (bathroom-only qualifier); E101 spec #18 and symbol legend; G400 detail 02; A530 general note F; coordination_issues C-03

c75186d67506.instanceNote: DB GAP — no row exists, but this is the classic guestroom punch item and it is worth its own line. WHAT IS NOT PUNCHABLE YET: the only device colour printed anywhere in the set is WHITE, and only at the microwave outlet (keynote 36). Everywhere else E101 spec #14 says device colour/style is 'coordinated with architect' and General Note 2 says 'clarify switch/receptacle/data-tel/TV outlet brand with franchise/owner before ordering' without naming a colour, series or plate style. There is nothing to punch a colour against until ironstack.pro produces the approved wiring-device submittal. WHAT IS PUNCHABLE TODAY: internal consistency (one series and colour across the room, the bath and room-to-room down the corridor), plates flat and tight, ganged devices under a single plate, and the 20 A rating per E101 General Note 10. Also enforceable and commonly missed: E400 General Note 1 and E101 spec #28 prohibit back-to-back boxes and require at least 6" separation (24" at fire/acoustic-rated walls) — 101's demising wall is W5 (1 HR, STC 56) and its corridor wall is W4 (1 HR, STC 54).
c75186d67506.where: Every device in the room and bath
c75186d67506.label: Wiring devices and cover plates generally — one consistent series and colour, all devices 20 A
c75186d67506.verifyAtPunch: Sight down the room — one plate colour and series throughout, all flat and square, no drywall gaps and no paint bridging the plate to the wall; confirm ganged devices share one plate; confirm no device box is back-to-back with the adjacent room's.
c75186d67506.src: E101 spec #14, #25, #28, #29 and General Notes #2, #7, #10; A555 keynote 36 (WHITE at the microwave); G402 bath GN1; E400 General Notes 1 and 2; A300 (W4/W5 ratings)

2aafc32bc625.verifyAtPunch: Count the DUPLEX and the QUAD receptacles separately and write both numbers down; plug-test every one for correct polarity and ground; trip the AFCI at the panel and confirm it kills them; measure and record the centreline height of one on each wall.
2aafc32bc625.src: E400 (layout; counts on the PDF only); E101 spec #18/#25/#14 and GN #10 (all devices 20 A) and symbol legend; A555 views 04 and 04.1; A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND (duplex, duplex-GFI, quad, quad-GFI); A530 general notes D and F; G400 detail 02; coordination_issues C-03
2aafc32bc625.label: Convenience receptacles — DUPLEX and QUAD, tamper-resistant, 20 A, Hubbell or approved equal
2aafc32bc625.instanceNote: QTY IS NOT STATED ON ANY SHEET — 1 is emitted as a placeholder, NOT as a count. No transcribed source states how many convenience receptacles a guestroom gets; E400 and the A555 view-04/04.1 plans are the only device layouts and their counts live on the source PDFs (packages/electrical.md open item 14, 'no takeoff attempted'). PULL THE COUNT OFF THE E400 / A555 PDF BEFORE THE WALK or the walker has no baseline. DEVICE TYPE IS ALSO UNSTATED — CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT, which assumed duplex throughout: the A550/A555 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND prints FOUR receptacle symbols — 'OUTLET - DUPLEX', 'OUTLET - DUPLEX - GFI', 'OUTLET - QUAD' and 'OUTLET - QUAD - GFI' — and E101's symbol legend independently carries a quad/quad-duplex receptacle. Which symbol lands at each dimensioned point on view 04.1 is readable only off the PDF. COUNT AND RECORD DUPLEX AND QUAD SEPARATELY. ROOM-101-SPECIFIC: 101 is the CONNECTOR variant, so it reads off A555 view 04.1 'ELEC.
